 2026 Voter Guide 
 What You Need to Know
 The purple battleground state of Pennsylvania is once again expected to play a critical role in determining which political party will secure a congressional majority.
 In addition to the commonwealth’s 17 congressional seats, Gov. Josh Shapiro, a Democrat, is running for reelection. His challenger is Republican state Treasurer Stacy Garrity.
 This guide doesn’t include the 203 state House and 25 state Senate seats up for grabs. Neither of Pennsylvania’s U.S. senators is up for election in 2026.

 Important Dates
 October 19 
 Last day to register before the November election
 October 27 
 Last day to apply for a mail-in or civilian absentee ballot
 November 3 
 Last day for county election offices to received completed mail-in and civilian ballots. (Must be received by 8 p.m.)
 November 3 
 Election Day!
 November 10 
 Last day for county election offices to receive completed military and overseas absentee ballots (submitted for delivery no later than 11:59 p.m. on Nov. 2)
 How-To
 Check your voter registration or apply 
 The Department of State lets you check your voter registration status by using your name, PA driver's license or PennDOT ID number.
 The last day to register to vote is Oct. 19.
 Applications to register can be submitted online or by contacting your county voter registration office.
 How to request a mail-in ballot 
 There are two ways to apply for a mail-in ballot: online or by visiting your local county board of elections. To find the later, navigate to your county on this Department of State website . You can also download a paper application and mail it in. 
 To fill out the state's online application , you'll need a valid PA driver's license or PennDOT ID number. If you don't have one of those numbers, you can just the last four digits of your Social Security number and upload your signature.
 Completed applications must be received by county officials by 5 p.m. on Oct. 27. Mail-in and absentee ballots must be returned by 8 p.m. on Election Day. 
 Track your ballot here .
 Find your polling place 
 Find your polling place so you can make a plan to vote. 
 Become a poll worker 
 Pennsylvania needs roughly 45,000 poll workers to staff more than 9,000 polling places. They're responsible for opening voting machines, checking in voters, closing up at the end of the night and more. 
 If you're interested, fill out the poll worker interest form and your county's election office will contact you.
